scope: Direct trace of world pointer handling, app input forwarding and the current low-level interaction dispatcher; no new browser invocation.

observed_code.finding: Entity actions are disabled when their current immediate permission is false. A primary click on the disabled first action only calls show; it sends neither movement nor a deferred interaction. Ground Take is similarly disabled by current canTake.
The shell forwards the picked world target to the UI. It does not retain an approach-and-act request.

Ordinary low-level interactions require the current source target/range before applying the interaction. Direct in-range requests work; this inspected path does not queue the requested action after movement.

qualification: Current immediate permission is not a substitute for the source menu behavior that approaches an interactable before executing its requested action.
The headless runner explicitly approaches targets with separate observed walk/door steps; its success does not prove the missing single-click browser behavior.
No new runtime click, renderer pick or original-server observation was performed for this code-trace record.
Existing low-level range/guard rejection is not itself permission to weaken authority or invent a client success.
required_work: A typed source approach-and-act path preserving the selected target/action/item identity and all non-range source permissions.
Rust/WASM interaction-state ownership and authoritative geometry/guards; do not parse denial prose or recreate game rules in UI TypeScript.
